action.mutates: replaces /var/tmp/p8test-fs-health with the mount point of a 16 MB ext4 image (/run/p8test-fsh/img on a loop device) holding f1, f2 and sub/f3 (8 KB each, NFILES 3 so every file is read); mounts it read-only three times: through a device-mapper device p8test-fsh whose table maps f1's blocks to the error target, then the subdirectory's block, then the plain loop device; the kernel logs the I/O errors; everything is unmounted and removed afterwards; the outputs go to /run/p8test-fsh/out.txt

outcomes.outcome: the per-volume check script carries the base directory, the size threshold and the file count, and nagios may run it through sudo
an empty tree (at or under the size threshold) is reported CRITICAL with exit 2
a readable tree above the threshold is listed, a sample of its files read, and reported OK with exit 0, also when nagios runs it through sudo
a file whose content cannot be read, or a tree that cannot be listed (I/O errors on the volume), is reported CRITICAL with exit 2; the intact volume is OK
only nagios may run the check through sudo without a password
